inputs.ttm_to_2026_06: Revenue 5,534.0; EBITDA (IFRS-16, pre-lease) 1,364.7 (24.7%); PBT 833.8; attributable NI 622.5; EPS ~0.53. H1 FY2026 vs H1 FY2025: revenue +7.0%, EBITDA margin 22.7% vs 28.8%, same-store sales -12.5%, restaurants 824 vs 807 at Dec-25 (+17 net in the half vs +140 net in FY2025).
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in RMB, the currency of the flows: China 10y CGB ~1.8% + beta ~1.1 x China equity risk premium ~6.5% + ~1.5-2pp premium for a Dec-2024 IPO, founder-controlled, HK-listed small/mid-cap in a deflationary consumer market = cost of equity ~11%; net cash, so WACC ~10.5%. Same WACC in all three scenarios -- cyclicality and the SSS reset are priced in the flows and the weights, not in the rate (charge risk once).
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) leases as operating cost. Full lease cash (capital + interest elements of lease liabilities, both from the financing section of the cash-flow statement: FY2025 248.578 + 39.859 = 288.437 = 5.40% of revenue; FY2024 264.922 = 5.08%; FY2023 200.286 = 4.40%; H1 FY2026 150.961 = 5.20%) charged inside EBITDA via lease_cost_pct_path. Lease liabilities (773.382 at 30 Jun 2026) excluded from net debt. ebitda_margin_path is on the stored IFRS-16 basis (PBT + finance costs + ALL D&A incl. right-of-use depreciation: FY2025 1,486.106 = 27.8%), and da_pct_path is depreciation and amortisation of OTHER assets only (FY2025 189.431 = 3.54%), so the lease is charged exactly once and cash-tax EBIT is after ex-ROU D&A. Cross-check: FY2025 EBITDA 1,486.1 - lease cash 288.4 = 1,197.7 vs the company's own Adjusted EBITDA 1,207.7; FY2025 EBIT on this basis 1,008.3 vs PBT 985.6 + finance costs 43.1 + ROU dep 268.0 - lease cash 288.4 = 1,008.3 (ties).
inputs.nci_treatment: Immaterial: RMB 2.5m contributed by a minority in H1 FY2026, loss share -0.47m. Flows are consolidated, no NCI deduction in the bridge. Revisit if the multi-brand JVs grow.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (operating company, non-US consumer, material leases) per .claude/skills/dcf-methods, with the adaptations file applied: RMB-built WACC, CNY flows vs HKD quote, lease treatment (B), SBC-zero market, matching-asset rule (interest income stripped, cash + time deposits + bank WMPs all in the bridge). Fresh build -- first valuation of this ticker; the drivers were drawn from the FY2024/FY2025 annual reports and the H1 FY2026 interim; 0999.HK_Analysis.json (written in parallel) was read before finalising and did not move any driver: its cited FY2026 broker net-profit estimate (~RMB 580m, Industrial Securities) ties to the base FY2026 build (EBIT ~799 x 0.73 + stripped investment income ~ RMB 595m) within 3%, and its ~907-store year-end estimate matches the base rollout pace. Operating history is short: IPO Dec 2024, full statements FY2023-FY2025 plus H1 FY2026, FY2022 from the five-year summary only. Horizon 10 years because FY2026 is a margin-reset year and the owner-FCF margin is still recovering at year 5. Cash tax 27% vs PRC statutory 25%: the Cayman holdco pays out most of its profit (FY2025 dividends 624m) and the PRC dividend withholding tax leaks through cash tax (FY2025 cash tax paid 290.5 = 29.5% of PBT; P&L rate 27.4%). Working capital: restaurant chain with payables + contract liabilities (prepaid cards) > receivables + inventory, so growth releases a little cash -- wc_capture 3% of the revenue change. The RMB 250m interim dividend (RMB 0.2139/share) was paid 15 Sep 2026, after the 30 Jun balance sheet and before the valuation date, and is deducted in the equity bridge; this also partly offsets the overlap between H1 FY2026 cash already in the bridge and the full FY2026 flow in year 1.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case FY2026-FY2030 average revenue growth. History is too short and too distorted to anchor on: FY2022 is a five-year-summary row (revenue 3,213 -> 5,345 is 18.5%/yr but FY2022 was a lockdown year), the equity CAGR is inflated by the Dec-2024 IPO proceeds (RMB 780m), and the EPS CAGR is diluted by the 17% post-IPO share-count step-up. The H1 FY2026 run-rate (+7% revenue, -12.5% same-store sales) is the better anchor.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR 95.9% vs revenue 18.5% / net income 44.4%: diverges >30% because FY2022 equity (325) preceded the IPO raise and the FY2023-24 pre-IPO dividend policy; not a signal about the business. Owner-FCF 2yr CAGR (15.5%) is below reported FCF (17.0%) because lease cash grew from 4.4% to 5.4% of revenue -- the store rollout is increasingly rent-funded.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = reported FCF - lease principal - lease interest - interest income - SBC(0). FY2023: 555.8 - 172.1 - 28.2 - 9.0 = 346.5. FY2024: 584.1 - 225.7 - 39.2 - 24.6 = 294.6. FY2025: 761.1 - 248.6 - 39.9 - 10.4 = 462.3. CAGRs over 2 years only (FY2023->FY2025); 5-year figures do not exist.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +6%: H1 was +7.0% and H2 FY2025 (2,631) was already below H1 FY2025 (2,714), so H2 laps an easier comp with ~8% more stores and a mid-single-digit SSS decline. FY2027-28 +8%: openings resume at ~100-150/yr on a 824-store base (prospectus plan was ~180/200 for 2026/27; H1 FY2026 net adds were only +17) with SSS flat-to-slightly-positive once the FY2026 price cuts annualise. Decelerating to 3% by year 10 as the mass-market Anhui-cuisine format saturates its advantaged regions.
base.margin_rationale: EBITDA (IFRS-16 basis) 23.0% in FY2026 (H1 22.7%) after the deliberate price reset and staff-cost step-up (+24% on +7% revenue); partial recovery to 25.5% by FY2030 via table-turn gains (3.3x vs 3.1x) and procurement/central-kitchen scale, deliberately held below the FY2025 27.8% peak which was flattered by H1 FY2025's 28.8%. Lease cash held at 5.2-5.3% (FY2025 5.4%, H1 FY2026 5.2%). Capex 6.5% while the rollout continues, tapering to 4.5% (D&A 3.6% plus modest growth). Cash tax 27% = 25% statutory + PRC dividend withholding leakage on a near-full payout.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2026 is a reset year the company chose: it cut prices ('passing on benefits to consumers') to defend traffic in a deflationary mass-market, so same-store sales fell 12.5% in H1 even as table turns rose to 3.3x, and staff costs rose 24% on 7% revenue. The base case has the price reset annualising by mid-FY2027, store openings resuming at 100-150 a year from 824 (the H1 FY2026 net add of 17 is treated as a pause, not the new pace), delivery continuing to shrink as a share of sales by design, and the IFRS-16 EBITDA margin recovering only to 25.5% -- not the FY2025 27.8% peak. Lease cash stays at ~5.2% of revenue; capex tapers from 6.5% to 4.5% as the rollout matures. The RMB 1.5bn net cash (mostly bank WMPs) and the near-full payout are the balance-sheet backstop.
scenario_narratives.bull: Value-for-money positioning wins share through the downturn: traffic gains outlast the price cuts, SSS turns positive in FY2027 on the lower base, openings return to the prospectus pace (~180-200/yr) including the Southeast Asia pilot and a second brand, and procurement/central-kitchen scale takes the margin back to 27.5%. Lease cost per store falls as landlords concede rent in a soft property market. Growth compounds at 8-11% for four years and the terminal growth is 3%.
scenario_narratives.bear: China catering deflation persists and competitors match the price cuts, so the SSS decline (already -9.4% in FY2025 before the -12.5% in H1 FY2026, with average dine-in spend down from RMB 57.1 to 50.5) is structural rather than a one-year reset: revenue growth stalls at 2-3% with openings offset by closures, the margin settles at 21.5-22% (H1 FY2026 was 22.7% and falling), rent ratchets to 5.8% of revenue as weaker stores de-leverage their leases, and capex collapses to maintenance. Terminal growth 2% and a 12x cap. Not a solvency case -- net cash and a 3.3x table turn keep it profitable -- but a value trap in which the owner-FCF margin is permanently ~6-7%.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: the last reported half shows -12.5% same-store sales, a 6pp EBITDA-margin contraction and net openings near zero, on a two-year listed history in a deflationary consumer market, so a structural (not one-off) reset is a live possibility. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs SSS recovery, a resumed rollout and margin repair to all land together while the industry is cutting price. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF on a lease-adjusted basis: the only cash flow a shareholder can take out of a restaurant chain is what remains after rent, so lease principal and interest are charged against EBITDA and lease liabilities are left out of net debt. RMB flows, RMB WACC, converted to HKD once at the end. Net cash is counted at the balance-sheet value of cash, time deposits and bank WMPs with their income stripped from the flows. The margin path deliberately capitalises a level below the FY2025 peak, because that peak preceded a self-inflicted price reset whose durability is unknown.
key_risks_to_valuation: Same-store sales: H1 FY2026 -12.5%; if the price reset does not restore traffic, the base margin recovery to 25.5% does not happen (bear = 22%).
Rollout pace: net adds fell from +140 in FY2025 to +17 in H1 FY2026; the base assumes 100-150/yr resumes.
Rent and labour leverage: lease cash rose from 4.4% to 5.4% of revenue FY2023-25 and staff costs 24.6% -> 28.5% of revenue H1-on-H1; both ratchet in a weak-SSS world.
Capital allocation: RMB 1.5bn net cash parked in bank wealth-management products, funded partly by RMB 560m of short-term bank loans; valued at book, with the carry stripped from the flows.
Short history: two full post-IPO years; FY2022 is a summary row; no Analysis JSON was available when the scenarios were drawn.
FX: HKD values move with CNY/HKD; the rate is dated and will not be refreshed by a price-only update.
